description: Analyze X-ray diffraction data from raw diffractogram through peak identification, phase matching, Rietveld refinement, and crystallite size estimation to a final XRD report.

steps.description: Import raw XRD data files and convert to a standardized two-theta vs intensity format.

inputs.name: raw-data-files
inputs.desc: Raw diffractometer output files (XRDML, RAW, or CSV)

inputs.name: instrument-parameters
inputs.desc: Wavelength, slit widths, scan range, step size

outputs.name: diffractogram
outputs.desc: Standardized two-theta vs intensity data

outputs.name: acquisition-metadata
outputs.desc: Instrument settings and scan conditions

process: Parse the raw data file format and extract intensity vs two-theta values
Validate angular range, step size, and count statistics
Normalize intensity units and flag any detector saturation or dropout regions
Export the clean diffractogram with acquisition metadata attached

steps.description: Remove background signal from the diffractogram to isolate diffraction peaks.

inputs.name: diffractogram
inputs.desc: Standardized two-theta vs intensity data

inputs.name: background-method
inputs.desc: Method selection: polynomial, spline, or Sonneveld-Visser

outputs.name: stripped-diffractogram
outputs.desc: Background-subtracted intensity data

outputs.name: background-curve
outputs.desc: The fitted background for inspection

process: Estimate the background using the selected method with iterative fitting
Subtract the background curve from the raw diffractogram
Verify that no negative intensities result and that peak shapes are preserved
Record the background model parameters for reproducibility

steps.description: Locate and characterize peaks in the background-stripped diffractogram.

inputs.name: stripped-diffractogram
inputs.desc: Background-subtracted intensity data

inputs.name: peak-detection-threshold
inputs.desc: Minimum intensity or signal-to-noise ratio for peak acceptance

outputs.name: peak-list
outputs.desc: Table of peak positions (two-theta), intensities, and FWHM values

outputs.name: peak-fit-residuals
outputs.desc: Goodness-of-fit metrics for each peak profile

process: Detect candidate peaks using second-derivative or wavelet methods
Fit each peak with a Voigt or pseudo-Voigt profile to extract position, intensity, and width
Filter peaks below the acceptance threshold
Produce the final peak list sorted by two-theta position

steps.description: Match observed peaks against crystallographic reference databases to identify phases.

inputs.name: peak-list
inputs.desc: Table of peak positions, intensities, and FWHM values

inputs.name: candidate-phases
inputs.desc: Optional list of expected phases to prioritize in the search

outputs.name: phase-identification
outputs.desc: Matched phases with confidence scores and reference card numbers

outputs.name: unmatched-peaks
outputs.desc: Peaks not assigned to any identified phase

process: Search the reference database (ICDD PDF, COD, or AMCSD) by peak position and relative intensity
Rank candidate phases by figure-of-merit score
Assign each observed peak to the best matching phase
Flag unmatched peaks for further investigation

steps.description: Refine crystal structure parameters and quantify phase fractions using Rietveld whole-pattern fitting.

inputs.name: diffractogram
inputs.desc: Standardized two-theta vs intensity data

inputs.name: phase-identification
inputs.desc: Matched phases with starting structural models

outputs.name: refined-parameters
outputs.desc: Lattice parameters, atomic positions, site occupancies, and thermal factors per phase

outputs.name: phase-fractions
outputs.desc: Weight percent of each phase with uncertainty

process: Load starting structural models for each identified phase
Refine instrument parameters (zero shift, sample displacement) followed by structural parameters
Monitor Rwp, Rexp, and chi-squared to assess fit quality
Extract phase fractions from scale factors and report with uncertainties

steps.description: Estimate average crystallite size and microstrain from peak broadening using the Scherrer equation and Williamson-Hall analysis.

inputs.name: peak-list
inputs.desc: Table of peak positions, intensities, and FWHM values

inputs.name: instrument-broadening
inputs.desc: Instrumental broadening profile from a standard reference material

outputs.name: crystallite-size
outputs.desc: Estimated crystallite size per phase with uncertainty

outputs.name: microstrain-estimate
outputs.desc: Microstrain contribution to broadening if resolved

process: Correct observed peak widths for instrumental broadening
Apply the Scherrer equation to individual peaks for a size estimate
Construct a Williamson-Hall plot to separate size and strain contributions
Report average crystallite size and microstrain with confidence intervals

steps.description: Compile all XRD analysis results into a structured report with annotated diffractograms and tables.

inputs.name: phase-identification
inputs.desc: Matched phases with confidence scores

inputs.name: refined-parameters
inputs.desc: Lattice parameters and phase fractions

inputs.name: crystallite-size
inputs.desc: Size and microstrain estimates

outputs.name: xrd-report
outputs.desc: Final report with annotated plots, phase table, and conclusions

outputs.name: supplementary-data
outputs.desc: Rietveld fit plots, residual curves, and raw peak data

process: Assemble the annotated diffractogram showing identified peaks and phases
Tabulate phase fractions, lattice parameters, and crystallite sizes
Write the interpretation section linking results to the sample context
Package the supplementary fit data for archival

description: Analyze tensile test data from raw stress-strain curves through yield, UTS, elongation, and modulus extraction to a mechanical testing report.

steps.description: Import raw tensile test data and convert force-displacement to engineering stress-strain.

inputs.name: raw-test-files
inputs.desc: Machine output files with force, displacement, and time

inputs.name: specimen-dimensions
inputs.desc: Gauge length, cross-sectional area, and geometry for each specimen

outputs.name: stress-strain-curves
outputs.desc: Engineering stress vs engineering strain for each specimen

outputs.name: test-metadata
outputs.desc: Strain rate, temperature, machine compliance correction applied

process: Parse raw force-displacement data from the testing machine format
Apply machine compliance correction if a compliance calibration is provided
Convert force to engineering stress and displacement to engineering strain using specimen dimensions
Align curves to zero stress and zero strain at the origin

steps.description: Determine yield strength using the 0.2% offset method or other specified criteria.

inputs.name: stress-strain-curves
inputs.desc: Engineering stress vs engineering strain per specimen

inputs.name: yield-method
inputs.desc: Offset percentage (default 0.2%) or proportional limit criterion

outputs.name: yield-strengths
outputs.desc: Yield strength per specimen with the offset line coordinates

outputs.name: elastic-region-fit
outputs.desc: Linear fit parameters for the elastic portion of each curve

process: Identify the linear elastic region of each curve by maximum R-squared linear fit
Construct the offset line parallel to the elastic slope shifted by the specified strain offset
Find the intersection of the offset line with the stress-strain curve
Record the yield strength and flag any specimens with ambiguous or discontinuous yielding

steps.description: Extract ultimate tensile strength and elongation at break from each stress-strain curve.

inputs.name: stress-strain-curves
inputs.desc: Engineering stress vs engineering strain per specimen

inputs.name: test-metadata
inputs.desc: Strain rate and temperature for context

outputs.name: uts-values
outputs.desc: Ultimate tensile strength per specimen

outputs.name: elongation-at-break
outputs.desc: Percent elongation at fracture per specimen

process: Find the maximum stress point on each curve to determine UTS
Identify the fracture point as the terminal data point or the point of sudden load drop
Compute total elongation at break as the strain at fracture times 100
Flag any specimens that fractured outside the gauge section

steps.description: Compute the elastic modulus from the slope of the linear elastic region of each curve.

inputs.name: stress-strain-curves
inputs.desc: Engineering stress vs engineering strain per specimen

inputs.name: elastic-region-fit
inputs.desc: Linear fit parameters identifying the elastic region bounds

outputs.name: elastic-moduli
outputs.desc: Young's modulus per specimen with R-squared of the fit

outputs.name: modulus-statistics
outputs.desc: Mean, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation across specimens

process: Use the previously identified elastic region bounds for each specimen
Compute the slope of the linear fit within those bounds
Report the modulus with the fit quality metric
Compute summary statistics across all specimens

steps.description: Compare mechanical properties across specimens and test conditions.

inputs.name: yield-strengths
inputs.desc: Yield strength per specimen

inputs.name: uts-values
inputs.desc: UTS per specimen

inputs.name: elastic-moduli
inputs.desc: Young's modulus per specimen

outputs.name: comparison-table
outputs.desc: Side-by-side property comparison with statistical tests

outputs.name: property-distributions
outputs.desc: Histograms and box plots of each property

process: Tabulate all mechanical properties by specimen and group (material, condition, orientation)
Compute group means, standard deviations, and confidence intervals
Run statistical comparisons (t-test or ANOVA) between groups if multiple conditions exist
Generate comparison plots showing property distributions by group

steps.description: Assess necking behavior and ductile-to-brittle failure characteristics from the stress-strain curve shape.

inputs.name: stress-strain-curves
inputs.desc: Engineering stress vs engineering strain per specimen

inputs.name: uts-values
inputs.desc: UTS per specimen to identify post-UTS region

outputs.name: necking-assessment
outputs.desc: Onset strain, reduction in area if measured, and failure mode classification

outputs.name: true-stress-strain
outputs.desc: True stress vs true strain curves computed up to necking onset

process: Identify the necking onset as the point where engineering stress begins to decrease after UTS
Compute the post-UTS elongation as a measure of necking extent
Convert engineering curves to true stress-strain up to the necking onset
Classify failure mode as ductile (cup-cone), brittle (flat fracture), or mixed

steps.description: Compile tensile testing results into a structured mechanical testing report.

inputs.name: comparison-table
inputs.desc: Property comparison across specimens

inputs.name: necking-assessment
inputs.desc: Failure mode classifications

inputs.name: test-metadata
inputs.desc: Test conditions and specimen information

outputs.name: tensile-report
outputs.desc: Final report with stress-strain plots, property tables, and conclusions

outputs.name: raw-data-archive
outputs.desc: All computed values in tabular format for further use

process: Assemble overlay stress-strain plots with key properties annotated
Build the property summary table with statistics and standard reference comparisons
Write the interpretation section covering material behavior and failure modes
Package raw data and computed values for archival

description: Analyze fluorescence spectroscopy data from raw spectra through quantum yield calculation, decay fitting, and FRET analysis to a fluorescence report.

steps.description: Import and organize raw excitation and emission spectra from the fluorimeter.

inputs.name: raw-spectra-files
inputs.desc: Fluorimeter output files with wavelength and intensity

inputs.name: sample-identifiers
inputs.desc: Sample names, concentrations, and solvent for each measurement

outputs.name: excitation-spectra
outputs.desc: Corrected excitation spectra per sample

outputs.name: emission-spectra
outputs.desc: Corrected emission spectra per sample

process: Parse fluorimeter output files and separate excitation from emission scans
Apply excitation source intensity correction using the reference detector signal
Organize spectra by sample identity and measurement condition
Flag any spectra with detector saturation or anomalous baselines

steps.description: Apply instrument response corrections to emission spectra for accurate intensity comparison.

inputs.name: emission-spectra
inputs.desc: Raw emission spectra per sample

inputs.name: instrument-response-function
inputs.desc: Wavelength-dependent detector and optics sensitivity curve

outputs.name: corrected-emission
outputs.desc: Instrument-corrected emission spectra

outputs.name: correction-factors
outputs.desc: Applied correction curve for documentation

process: Divide each emission spectrum by the instrument response function
Verify that the corrected spectrum of a known standard matches the published shape
Subtract solvent blank emission if measured
Record the correction factors applied for reproducibility

steps.description: Calculate fluorescence quantum yield using the comparative method with a known reference.

inputs.name: corrected-emission
inputs.desc: Instrument-corrected emission spectra for sample and reference

inputs.name: absorbance-values
inputs.desc: Absorbance at excitation wavelength for sample and reference

outputs.name: quantum-yield
outputs.desc: Absolute quantum yield with uncertainty per sample

outputs.name: calculation-details
outputs.desc: Integrated emission areas, refractive index corrections, and reference values used

process: Integrate emission spectra over the full emission band for both sample and reference
Apply the comparative quantum yield formula with refractive index correction
Verify that absorbance values are in the optically dilute regime (below 0.1)
Report quantum yield with propagated uncertainty from absorbance and integration

steps.description: Fit fluorescence lifetime decay curves to single or multi-exponential models.

inputs.name: decay-curves
inputs.desc: Time-resolved fluorescence intensity data per sample

inputs.name: instrument-response-function
inputs.desc: IRF measured under the same conditions

outputs.name: lifetime-fit-results
outputs.desc: Fitted lifetimes, amplitudes, and chi-squared per model per sample

outputs.name: residuals
outputs.desc: Weighted residuals and autocorrelation for fit quality assessment

process: Convolve candidate decay models with the IRF for iterative reconvolution fitting
Fit one-exponential, two-exponential, and stretched-exponential models
Select the best model by reduced chi-squared, residual randomness, and Durbin-Watson statistic
Report lifetimes and fractional amplitudes with confidence intervals

steps.description: Analyze Forster resonance energy transfer efficiency from donor-acceptor fluorescence data.

inputs.name: corrected-emission
inputs.desc: Emission spectra for donor-only, acceptor-only, and donor-acceptor samples

inputs.name: lifetime-fit-results
inputs.desc: Donor lifetimes in absence and presence of acceptor

outputs.name: fret-efficiency
outputs.desc: FRET efficiency calculated by intensity ratio and lifetime methods

outputs.name: distance-estimate
outputs.desc: Donor-acceptor distance from FRET efficiency using the Forster radius

process: Calculate FRET efficiency from donor quenching (intensity-based method)
Calculate FRET efficiency from donor lifetime shortening (lifetime-based method)
Estimate the donor-acceptor distance using the known Forster radius for the pair
Compare intensity and lifetime FRET values and note any discrepancy

steps.description: Compile all fluorescence analysis results into a final report with spectra, lifetime plots, and tables.

inputs.name: quantum-yield
inputs.desc: Quantum yield results per sample

inputs.name: lifetime-fit-results
inputs.desc: Lifetime and decay analysis results

inputs.name: fret-efficiency
inputs.desc: FRET efficiency and distance estimates if applicable

outputs.name: fluorescence-report
outputs.desc: Structured report with annotated spectra, decay fits, and quantitative summary

outputs.name: data-tables
outputs.desc: All computed photophysical parameters in tabular format

process: Assemble annotated emission spectra and decay curves for each sample
Build the summary table of quantum yields, lifetimes, and FRET parameters
Write the interpretation connecting photophysical behavior to sample properties
Package all data tables and fit parameters for archival

description: Compute and compare ecological diversity metrics from species abundance data through alpha and beta diversity, PERMANOVA, and rarefaction to a diversity report.

steps.description: Organize raw species observation data into a site-by-species abundance matrix.

inputs.name: observation-records
inputs.desc: Raw species observation data with site, species, and count

inputs.name: taxonomic-key
inputs.desc: Accepted species names and synonymy table for standardization

outputs.name: abundance-matrix
outputs.desc: Sites as rows, species as columns, counts as values

outputs.name: sampling-effort
outputs.desc: Number of samples, area surveyed, or time spent per site

process: Standardize species names using the taxonomic key to resolve synonyms and misspellings
Aggregate counts by site and species, resolving duplicate entries
Build the site-by-species abundance matrix
Record sampling effort per site for rarefaction normalization

steps.description: Calculate within-site diversity metrics: species richness, Shannon index, Simpson index, and evenness.

inputs.name: abundance-matrix
inputs.desc: Site-by-species abundance matrix

inputs.name: diversity-indices
inputs.desc: Which indices to compute (default: all standard indices)

outputs.name: alpha-diversity-table
outputs.desc: Richness, Shannon H, Simpson D, and Pielou evenness per site

outputs.name: confidence-intervals
outputs.desc: Bootstrap confidence intervals for each index per site

process: Count species richness (S) at each site
Compute Shannon entropy H and Simpson concentration D from proportional abundances
Compute Pielou evenness J = H / ln(S)
Bootstrap resample each site to generate confidence intervals for all indices

steps.description: Compute between-site dissimilarity using Bray-Curtis, Jaccard, and other distance metrics.

inputs.name: abundance-matrix
inputs.desc: Site-by-species abundance matrix

inputs.name: distance-metric
inputs.desc: Metric selection: Bray-Curtis (abundance) or Jaccard (presence-absence)

outputs.name: distance-matrix
outputs.desc: Pairwise site dissimilarity matrix

outputs.name: ordination-coordinates
outputs.desc: NMDS or PCoA coordinates for visualization

process: Compute the pairwise distance matrix using the selected metric
Run non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) or PCoA for ordination
Report stress (NMDS) or proportion of variance explained (PCoA)
Generate the ordination plot with sites colored by group

steps.description: Test whether community composition differs among groups using permutational multivariate ANOVA.

inputs.name: distance-matrix
inputs.desc: Pairwise site dissimilarity matrix

inputs.name: group-assignments
inputs.desc: Categorical grouping variable for each site (treatment, habitat, time)

outputs.name: permanova-results
outputs.desc: F-statistic, R-squared, and p-value from the permutation test

outputs.name: dispersion-test
outputs.desc: PERMDISP results testing homogeneity of group dispersions

process: Partition the distance matrix sums-of-squares by group using PERMANOVA
Run the specified number of permutations (default 999) to generate the null distribution
Test multivariate dispersion homogeneity (PERMDISP) to validate PERMANOVA assumptions
Report F, R-squared, p-value, and note if dispersion differences complicate interpretation

steps.description: Generate rarefaction and extrapolation curves to compare diversity at equal sampling effort.

inputs.name: abundance-matrix
inputs.desc: Site-by-species abundance matrix

inputs.name: sampling-effort
inputs.desc: Effort data per site for standardization

outputs.name: rarefaction-curves
outputs.desc: Sample-based or individual-based rarefaction curves per site

outputs.name: estimated-richness
outputs.desc: Chao1 or ACE estimated total species richness per site

process: Compute the rarefaction curve for each site by subsampling without replacement
Extrapolate beyond observed effort using the Chao1 or iNEXT method
Plot rarefaction and extrapolation curves with 95% confidence bands
Report asymptotic richness estimates and sample completeness ratios

steps.description: Compile all diversity analysis results into a structured ecology report.

inputs.name: alpha-diversity-table
inputs.desc: Within-site diversity indices

inputs.name: permanova-results
inputs.desc: Between-group composition test results

inputs.name: rarefaction-curves
inputs.desc: Rarefaction and richness estimation results

outputs.name: diversity-report
outputs.desc: Final report with diversity tables, ordination plots, and rarefaction curves

outputs.name: analysis-archive
outputs.desc: All matrices, statistics, and computed indices for reproducibility

process: Assemble diversity summary tables and ordination figures
Present PERMANOVA and dispersion test results with ecological interpretation
Include rarefaction curves showing sampling adequacy
Package all computed data for archival and reproducibility

description: Determine a chemical reaction mechanism through intermediate identification, kinetics measurement, energy profiling, isotope labeling, DFT comparison, and mechanism proposal.

steps.description: Identify reaction products and intermediates using spectroscopic and chromatographic techniques.

inputs.name: reaction-mixture-samples
inputs.desc: Time-resolved aliquots from the reaction at various conversions

inputs.name: analytical-methods
inputs.desc: Available techniques: NMR, MS, IR, UV-Vis, GC, HPLC

outputs.name: intermediate-catalog
outputs.desc: List of detected species with structural assignments and retention times or chemical shifts

outputs.name: temporal-profiles
outputs.desc: Concentration vs time profiles for each identified species

process: Analyze aliquots by the selected analytical methods at each time point
Assign molecular structures to detected signals using spectral databases and fragmentation patterns
Track the appearance and disappearance of each species over time
Build the temporal concentration profile for starting material, intermediates, and products

steps.description: Measure reaction kinetics under systematically varied conditions to determine rate laws.

inputs.name: temporal-profiles
inputs.desc: Concentration vs time data for reactants and products

inputs.name: experimental-conditions
inputs.desc: Temperature, solvent, catalyst loading, and reagent concentrations tested

outputs.name: rate-law
outputs.desc: Rate expression with reaction orders for each reactant and the rate constant

outputs.name: activation-parameters
outputs.desc: Activation energy (Arrhenius) or enthalpy and entropy of activation (Eyring)

process: Fit concentration-time data to integrated rate expressions (zeroth, first, second order)
Determine reaction order with respect to each reactant by the method of initial rates or excess
Measure rate constants at multiple temperatures
Construct Arrhenius or Eyring plots to extract activation parameters

steps.description: Construct the free energy profile of the reaction pathway showing intermediates and transition states.

inputs.name: rate-law
inputs.desc: Rate expression with rate constants

inputs.name: activation-parameters
inputs.desc: Activation energies or Eyring parameters

outputs.name: energy-profile
outputs.desc: Free energy diagram with barriers, intermediates, and products

outputs.name: rate-determining-step
outputs.desc: Identification of the highest barrier step

process: Convert rate constants to free energy barriers using transition state theory
Place intermediates at their relative free energies based on equilibrium data if available
Construct the energy profile diagram from reactants to products
Identify the rate-determining step as the highest energy transition state

steps.description: Design and interpret isotope labeling experiments to test proposed mechanistic pathways.

inputs.name: proposed-mechanism
inputs.desc: Candidate mechanistic steps to be tested

inputs.name: available-labels
inputs.desc: Isotopes available: deuterium, 13C, 15N, 18O

outputs.name: labeling-predictions
outputs.desc: Where each label should appear in products for each candidate mechanism

outputs.name: experimental-results
outputs.desc: Observed label distribution in products compared to predictions

process: For each candidate mechanism, trace where the isotopic label would end up in products
Design the labeling experiment to distinguish between competing pathways
Analyze the labeled products by mass spectrometry or NMR to determine label position
Compare observed labeling pattern against predictions to rule out or support each pathway

steps.description: Compare experimental mechanistic findings with DFT computational results for transition states and intermediates.

inputs.name: energy-profile
inputs.desc: Experimental free energy diagram

inputs.name: dft-calculations
inputs.desc: Computed structures, energies, and vibrational frequencies for intermediates and transition states

outputs.name: experiment-theory-comparison
outputs.desc: Side-by-side comparison of experimental and computed barriers and geometries

outputs.name: agreement-assessment
outputs.desc: Quantitative agreement metrics and discrepancies noted

process: Align computational and experimental species by structure correspondence
Compare computed barriers with experimental activation parameters
Assess whether computed transition state geometries are consistent with observed selectivity
Note discrepancies and suggest whether the computational level of theory is adequate

steps.description: Synthesize all evidence into a coherent proposed mechanism with confidence assessment.

inputs.name: intermediate-catalog
inputs.desc: Detected intermediates and their temporal profiles

inputs.name: rate-law
inputs.desc: Kinetic rate expression

inputs.name: experimental-results
inputs.desc: Isotope labeling results

outputs.name: proposed-mechanism
outputs.desc: Arrow-pushing mechanism with elementary steps consistent with all evidence

outputs.name: evidence-summary
outputs.desc: Which evidence supports each step and what remains ambiguous

process: Write the elementary steps consistent with the rate law and observed intermediates
Verify that isotope labeling results match the proposed pathway
Check that the proposed rate-determining step matches the observed activation parameters
Identify any remaining ambiguities and suggest experiments to resolve them

steps.description: Compile the mechanism elucidation study into a final report with energy profiles and evidence tables.

inputs.name: proposed-mechanism
inputs.desc: The proposed reaction mechanism

inputs.name: experiment-theory-comparison
inputs.desc: Agreement between experimental and computational results

inputs.name: evidence-summary
inputs.desc: Supporting evidence for each mechanistic step

outputs.name: mechanism-report
outputs.desc: Final report with mechanism scheme, energy profile, and evidence table

outputs.name: supporting-data
outputs.desc: All kinetic data, spectra, and computational results

process: Draw the complete mechanism scheme with arrow-pushing notation
Present the energy profile with experimental and computed values overlaid
Build the evidence table mapping each mechanistic claim to its supporting data
Package all raw kinetic data, spectra, and DFT output files

description: Analyze wind tunnel test data from raw force measurements through corrections, coefficient computation, CFD comparison, and flow feature identification to an aerodynamic report.

steps.description: Import raw force and moment balance data from the wind tunnel data acquisition system.

inputs.name: balance-data-files
inputs.desc: Multi-component balance output files with forces, moments, and freestream conditions

inputs.name: model-reference
inputs.desc: Reference area, length, and moment center coordinates

outputs.name: raw-forces-moments
outputs.desc: Six-component force and moment data at each test point

outputs.name: freestream-conditions
outputs.desc: Dynamic pressure, Mach number, Reynolds number, and angle of attack per point

process: Parse the data acquisition output and extract force, moment, and tunnel condition channels
Apply balance calibration matrix to convert raw voltages to engineering units
Associate each data point with its angle of attack and freestream conditions
Check for drift by comparing tare runs at the start and end of the test

steps.description: Apply standard corrections for wall interference, support tare, blockage, and buoyancy.

inputs.name: raw-forces-moments
inputs.desc: Uncorrected six-component data

inputs.name: tunnel-geometry
inputs.desc: Test section dimensions, slot or solid walls, support strut geometry

outputs.name: corrected-forces-moments
outputs.desc: Forces and moments with all corrections applied

outputs.name: correction-breakdown
outputs.desc: Magnitude of each correction for traceability

process: Subtract support strut tare loads measured with the metric part removed
Apply solid blockage and wake blockage corrections based on model and wake size
Correct for streamline curvature (wall interference) on lift, pitching moment, and angle of attack
Apply buoyancy correction for static pressure gradient along the test section

steps.description: Compute non-dimensional aerodynamic coefficients from corrected forces and freestream conditions.

inputs.name: corrected-forces-moments
inputs.desc: Corrected six-component data

inputs.name: model-reference
inputs.desc: Reference area, span, and mean aerodynamic chord

outputs.name: aero-coefficients
outputs.desc: CL, CD, CM, CY, Cl, Cn at each angle of attack

outputs.name: derived-quantities
outputs.desc: Lift-to-drag ratio, Oswald efficiency, and lift curve slope

process: Non-dimensionalize forces by dynamic pressure and reference area
Non-dimensionalize moments by dynamic pressure, reference area, and reference length
Compute derived quantities: L/D, dCL/dalpha, and induced drag factor
Tabulate all coefficients at each angle of attack

steps.description: Generate drag polar, lift curve, and moment curve plots from aerodynamic coefficients.

inputs.name: aero-coefficients
inputs.desc: CL, CD, CM at each angle of attack

inputs.name: comparison-data
inputs.desc: Reference data from previous tests or published results if available

outputs.name: aerodynamic-plots
outputs.desc: Drag polar (CL vs CD), lift curve (CL vs alpha), moment curve (CM vs alpha)

outputs.name: stall-characteristics
outputs.desc: CLmax, stall angle, and pitching moment break

process: Plot the drag polar (CL vs CD) with the ideal parabolic drag polar overlaid
Plot the lift curve (CL vs alpha) and determine CLmax and stall angle
Plot the pitching moment curve and identify the aerodynamic center or neutral point
Overlay comparison data if provided and annotate differences

steps.description: Compare wind tunnel results with CFD predictions to assess simulation accuracy.

inputs.name: aero-coefficients
inputs.desc: Experimental CL, CD, CM vs alpha

inputs.name: cfd-predictions
inputs.desc: CFD-computed coefficients at matching conditions

outputs.name: comparison-plots
outputs.desc: Overlay plots of experimental vs CFD coefficients

outputs.name: discrepancy-analysis
outputs.desc: Quantified differences and likely sources (turbulence model, transition, grid)

process: Interpolate experimental and CFD data to common angle-of-attack points
Compute absolute and percent differences for CL, CD, and CM
Plot experimental and CFD predictions on the same axes
Identify systematic trends in the discrepancies and suggest their likely sources

steps.description: Identify key flow features (separation, transition, vortex structures) from force data trends and flow visualization.

inputs.name: aero-coefficients
inputs.desc: CL, CD, CM vs alpha showing inflections or breaks

inputs.name: flow-visualization-data
inputs.desc: Oil flow, tuft, or PIV images if available

outputs.name: flow-features
outputs.desc: Identified separation onset, transition location, and vortex features

outputs.name: feature-evidence
outputs.desc: Which data (force break, visualization image) supports each identified feature

process: Examine the lift curve for nonlinearity that indicates flow separation onset
Look for drag bucket or drag rise that indicates laminar-to-turbulent transition
Correlate force data features with flow visualization evidence if available
Catalog each identified feature with its angle-of-attack range and evidence

steps.description: Compile all wind tunnel analysis into a final aerodynamic test report.

inputs.name: aerodynamic-plots
inputs.desc: Drag polar, lift curve, and moment plots

inputs.name: discrepancy-analysis
inputs.desc: Experimental vs CFD comparison

inputs.name: flow-features
inputs.desc: Identified flow features and their evidence

outputs.name: aerodynamic-report
outputs.desc: Final report with polars, comparison tables, and flow feature analysis

outputs.name: data-package
outputs.desc: All corrected coefficients and raw data in tabular format

process: Assemble the polars, comparison overlays, and flow visualization figures
Build the coefficient summary table at key angles of attack
Write the analysis section covering flow features and CFD agreement
Package all processed data for archival and future reference

description: Calibrate a paleoclimate proxy from modern calibration data through transfer function construction, validation, fossil record application, and uncertainty estimation to a paleoclimate reconstruction.

steps.description: Assemble paired modern proxy measurements and instrumental climate data for calibration.

inputs.name: modern-proxy-data
inputs.desc: Proxy measurements from modern samples (e.g., tree ring widths, foram isotopes, pollen counts)

inputs.name: instrumental-climate
inputs.desc: Corresponding instrumental temperature, precipitation, or other climate variable

outputs.name: calibration-dataset
outputs.desc: Paired proxy-climate values with site metadata

outputs.name: data-coverage-summary
outputs.desc: Spatial and temporal coverage of the calibration set

process: Match proxy sample locations and times to the nearest instrumental climate station or gridded product
Screen for outliers and verify that proxy-climate pairings are ecologically plausible
Document the spatial and temporal coverage of the calibration set
Split into calibration and verification subsets if the dataset is large enough

steps.description: Build the mathematical relationship between the proxy and the target climate variable.

inputs.name: calibration-dataset
inputs.desc: Paired proxy-climate values

inputs.name: method-choice
inputs.desc: Regression, weighted averaging (WA), modern analogue technique (MAT), or WA-PLS

outputs.name: transfer-function
outputs.desc: Fitted model relating proxy values to climate variable

outputs.name: calibration-statistics
outputs.desc: R-squared, RMSE, and number of components or analogues used

process: Fit the selected model using the calibration subset of data
Optimize model complexity (number of PLS components, number of analogues) using cross-validation
Report calibration statistics: R-squared, root mean square error of prediction
Save the fitted model parameters for application to fossil data

steps.description: Validate the transfer function against independent data not used in calibration.

inputs.name: transfer-function
inputs.desc: Fitted proxy-climate model

inputs.name: calibration-dataset
inputs.desc: Full dataset including the verification subset

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Verification R-squared, RMSE, and reduction of error (RE) statistic

outputs.name: residual-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Spatial and temporal patterns in residuals

process: Apply the transfer function to the withheld verification data
Compute verification statistics: R-squared, RMSEP, and RE or CE statistics
Examine residuals for spatial or temporal bias that would indicate model failure
Determine if the model passes standard validation thresholds (RE > 0)

steps.description: Apply the validated transfer function to fossil proxy data to reconstruct past climate.

inputs.name: transfer-function
inputs.desc: Validated proxy-climate model

inputs.name: fossil-proxy-data
inputs.desc: Down-core or time-series proxy measurements from the geological record

outputs.name: climate-reconstruction
outputs.desc: Reconstructed climate variable through time

outputs.name: analogue-quality
outputs.desc: Goodness-of-fit or analogue distance at each fossil sample

process: Apply the transfer function to each fossil sample to produce a climate estimate
Check whether each fossil assemblage has a good modern analogue in the calibration set
Flag samples with poor analogues or that fall outside the calibration range
Produce the raw reconstruction time series

steps.description: Quantify uncertainty in the paleoclimate reconstruction from calibration error, chronology, and sample-specific analogue quality.

inputs.name: climate-reconstruction
inputs.desc: Raw reconstructed climate time series

inputs.name: calibration-statistics
inputs.desc: RMSEP and model residual distribution

inputs.name: analogue-quality
inputs.desc: Per-sample analogue distance or fit metric

outputs.name: uncertainty-envelope
outputs.desc: Confidence bands around the reconstruction at each time point

outputs.name: uncertainty-decomposition
outputs.desc: Relative contributions of calibration, chronology, and analogue quality to total uncertainty

process: Apply the calibration RMSEP as a baseline uncertainty at every sample
Inflate uncertainty for samples with poor modern analogues
Incorporate chronological uncertainty if an age model with error estimates is provided
Produce the final reconstruction with upper and lower confidence bands

steps.description: Compile the calibration, validation, and reconstruction into a final paleoclimate report.

inputs.name: climate-reconstruction
inputs.desc: Reconstructed climate with uncertainty envelope

inputs.name: validation-results
inputs.desc: Transfer function validation statistics

inputs.name: uncertainty-decomposition
inputs.desc: Sources and magnitudes of uncertainty

outputs.name: paleoclimate-report
outputs.desc: Final report with reconstruction plot, validation summary, and interpretation

outputs.name: reconstruction-data
outputs.desc: Tabulated reconstruction values with uncertainties for archival

process: Plot the reconstruction time series with confidence bands and modern climate overlay
Summarize transfer function calibration and validation statistics
Interpret the reconstruction in the context of known climate events
Package the reconstruction data and transfer function for archival

description: Analyze cell viability assay data from plate reader import through normalization, dose-response fitting, assay quality assessment, and compound comparison to a viability report.

steps.description: Import plate reader data and map well positions to experimental conditions.

inputs.name: plate-reader-files
inputs.desc: Raw absorbance, fluorescence, or luminescence output from the plate reader

inputs.name: plate-layout
inputs.desc: Well-to-condition mapping: compound, concentration, and control assignments

outputs.name: mapped-readings
outputs.desc: Signal values linked to compound, concentration, and replicate identifiers

outputs.name: control-wells
outputs.desc: Identified positive control (100% viable) and negative control (0% viable) wells

process: Parse plate reader output and extract signal values indexed by well position
Map each well to its experimental condition using the plate layout
Identify and separate control wells (positive, negative, blank)
Flag any wells with anomalous readings (air bubbles, edge effects)

steps.description: Subtract blank, normalize signal to controls, and compute percent viability.

inputs.name: mapped-readings
inputs.desc: Signal values per well with condition labels

inputs.name: control-wells
inputs.desc: Positive and negative control signal values

outputs.name: percent-viability
outputs.desc: Viability as percentage of positive control per well

outputs.name: replicate-statistics
outputs.desc: Mean, standard deviation, and CV per concentration per compound

process: Subtract the mean blank (negative control) signal from all wells
Normalize each treated well to the mean positive control: viability = (treated - neg) / (pos - neg) x 100
Average replicates and compute standard deviation and coefficient of variation
Flag any concentration points with CV above 20% for review

steps.description: Fit dose-response curves and extract IC50 or EC50 values.

inputs.name: percent-viability
inputs.desc: Mean percent viability at each concentration

inputs.name: concentration-series
inputs.desc: Compound concentrations in molar units

outputs.name: dose-response-fit
outputs.desc: Fitted four-parameter logistic curve with IC50, Hill slope, top, and bottom

outputs.name: fit-quality
outputs.desc: R-squared, confidence intervals on IC50, and residual plot

process: Plot percent viability vs log concentration for each compound
Fit a four-parameter logistic (Hill) model to each compound's data
Extract IC50 (or EC50) with 95% confidence interval from the fit
Report Hill slope, top plateau, bottom plateau, and goodness of fit

steps.description: Assess assay quality using the Z-factor and control signal window.

inputs.name: control-wells
inputs.desc: Positive and negative control signal values

inputs.name: replicate-statistics
inputs.desc: Within-plate variability metrics

outputs.name: z-factor
outputs.desc: Z-factor score per plate indicating assay quality

outputs.name: quality-classification
outputs.desc: Pass (Z > 0.5), marginal (0 < Z < 0.5), or fail (Z < 0) per plate

process: Compute Z-factor from positive and negative control means and standard deviations
Classify each plate as excellent (Z > 0.5), acceptable (Z > 0), or failed
Check signal-to-background ratio and signal-to-noise ratio
Flag any plates that should be repeated due to poor assay performance

steps.description: Compare potency and efficacy across compounds or conditions.

inputs.name: dose-response-fit
inputs.desc: Fitted parameters (IC50, Hill slope, plateaus) per compound

inputs.name: percent-viability
inputs.desc: Normalized viability data for all compounds

outputs.name: potency-ranking
outputs.desc: Compounds ranked by IC50 with confidence intervals

outputs.name: selectivity-index
outputs.desc: Ratio of IC50 values between cell types if tested on multiple lines

process: Rank compounds by IC50 from most to least potent
Compute selectivity indices if data from multiple cell lines is available
Overlay dose-response curves on a single plot for visual comparison
Identify the lead compound(s) based on potency, efficacy, and selectivity criteria

steps.description: Compile all viability assay results into a structured pharmacology report.

inputs.name: potency-ranking
inputs.desc: Compound ranking with IC50 values

inputs.name: z-factor
inputs.desc: Assay quality scores

inputs.name: dose-response-fit
inputs.desc: Fitted curves and parameters

outputs.name: viability-report
outputs.desc: Final report with dose-response curves, potency table, and quality assessment

outputs.name: data-tables
outputs.desc: All raw and normalized data with fit parameters for archival

process: Assemble dose-response curve overlays and the potency ranking table
Include assay quality metrics and any plate exclusions with justification
Write the results interpretation identifying lead compounds and next steps
Package all raw plate data, normalized values, and fit parameters

description: Analyze rock mechanics test data from stress-strain import through strength determination, failure envelope construction, and rock mass classification to a geomechanics report.

steps.description: Import stress-strain data from uniaxial and triaxial compression tests on rock specimens.

inputs.name: test-data-files
inputs.desc: Load frame output: axial load, axial displacement, confining pressure, and lateral strain

inputs.name: specimen-log
inputs.desc: Specimen dimensions, lithology, depth, and test conditions

outputs.name: stress-strain-data
outputs.desc: Axial stress vs axial strain and lateral strain for each specimen at each confining pressure

outputs.name: specimen-metadata
outputs.desc: Specimen identity, dimensions, lithology, and test temperature

process: Parse load frame output and convert force and displacement to stress and strain
Apply area correction for barreling in unconfined tests if specimen aspect ratio is non-standard
Organize data by specimen and confining pressure level
Check for seating artifacts at low loads and trim if necessary

steps.description: Determine uniaxial compressive strength, Young's modulus, and Poisson's ratio from unconfined tests.

inputs.name: stress-strain-data
inputs.desc: Axial stress vs axial and lateral strain at zero confining pressure

inputs.name: specimen-metadata
inputs.desc: Specimen dimensions for correction

outputs.name: ucs-values
outputs.desc: Uniaxial compressive strength per specimen

outputs.name: elastic-properties
outputs.desc: Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio per specimen with method (tangent, secant, or average)

process: Identify peak axial stress as the uniaxial compressive strength (UCS)
Compute tangent Young's modulus at 50% of UCS from the axial stress-strain curve
Compute Poisson's ratio from the ratio of lateral to axial strain at the same stress level
Report mean and range across specimens

steps.description: Construct the Mohr-Coulomb failure envelope from triaxial test results at multiple confining pressures.

inputs.name: stress-strain-data
inputs.desc: Peak stress at each confining pressure

inputs.name: ucs-values
inputs.desc: Unconfined compressive strength as the zero-confinement data point

outputs.name: mohr-circles
outputs.desc: Mohr circle diagram with failure envelope

outputs.name: failure-envelope-fit
outputs.desc: Linear Mohr-Coulomb fit: cohesion (c) and friction angle (phi)

process: Plot Mohr circles for each test at its sigma-1 (peak axial stress) and sigma-3 (confining pressure)
Fit a linear failure envelope tangent to the circles
Extract cohesion (c) and internal friction angle (phi) from the envelope slope and intercept
Assess the quality of the linear fit and note if curvature suggests Hoek-Brown is more appropriate

steps.description: Compute Mohr-Coulomb and Hoek-Brown strength parameters with statistical confidence.

inputs.name: failure-envelope-fit
inputs.desc: Preliminary cohesion and friction angle from Mohr-Coulomb

inputs.name: mohr-circles
inputs.desc: All test data points for regression

outputs.name: strength-parameters
outputs.desc: Cohesion, friction angle, and Hoek-Brown constants (mi, sigci) with confidence intervals

outputs.name: parameter-comparison
outputs.desc: Mohr-Coulomb vs Hoek-Brown fit quality comparison

process: Perform least-squares regression on sigma-1 vs sigma-3 data for the linear Mohr-Coulomb fit
Fit the Hoek-Brown criterion to the same data and extract mi and sigci
Compare R-squared and residuals for both failure criteria
Report parameters with 95% confidence intervals from the regression

steps.description: Classify the rock mass using standard systems (RMR, Q-system, GSI) from lab and field data.

inputs.name: ucs-values
inputs.desc: Lab UCS and elastic property values

inputs.name: field-observations
inputs.desc: Joint spacing, condition, groundwater, RQD, and discontinuity data

outputs.name: rmr-rating
outputs.desc: Rock Mass Rating (RMR) score and class

outputs.name: q-value
outputs.desc: NGI Q-system value and support recommendation

process: Score each RMR parameter: UCS, RQD, joint spacing, joint condition, groundwater, and orientation adjustment
Sum for total RMR and classify (I through V)
Compute Q from RQD, Jn, Jr, Ja, Jw, and SRF parameters
Compare classifications and note any disagreements

steps.description: Compile all rock mechanics results into a geomechanics investigation report.

inputs.name: strength-parameters
inputs.desc: Mohr-Coulomb and Hoek-Brown parameters with confidence intervals

inputs.name: rmr-rating
inputs.desc: Rock mass classification scores

inputs.name: elastic-properties
inputs.desc: Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio

outputs.name: geomechanics-report
outputs.desc: Final report with Mohr diagrams, strength parameters, and rock mass classification

outputs.name: test-data-archive
outputs.desc: All stress-strain curves and computed parameters for archival

process: Assemble Mohr circle diagrams with fitted failure envelopes
Tabulate all strength and elastic parameters with specimen details
Present rock mass classification results with design implications
Package all raw test data and computed values

description: Analyze receptor-ligand binding data from raw binding curves through model fitting, Kd and Bmax extraction, competition analysis, and cooperativity testing to a binding report.

steps.description: Import raw radioligand or fluorescent ligand binding data and organize by experiment type.

inputs.name: binding-data-files
inputs.desc: Raw counts (CPM, DPM) or fluorescence values at each ligand concentration

inputs.name: experiment-design
inputs.desc: Saturation or competition format, nonspecific binding definition, replicate structure

outputs.name: specific-binding
outputs.desc: Total minus nonspecific binding at each concentration

outputs.name: experiment-metadata
outputs.desc: Ligand identity, receptor source, temperature, and incubation time

process: Parse raw data files and organize by ligand concentration and replicate
Subtract nonspecific binding (defined by excess cold ligand) from total to get specific binding
Average replicates and compute standard error
Check that the highest concentration approaches saturation for saturation experiments

steps.description: Fit saturation binding data to one-site, two-site, or Hill models.

inputs.name: specific-binding
inputs.desc: Specific binding vs free ligand concentration

inputs.name: model-candidates
inputs.desc: Models to test: one-site, two-site, Hill equation

outputs.name: fit-results
outputs.desc: Fitted parameters (Kd, Bmax, Hill coefficient) for each model with standard errors

outputs.name: model-selection
outputs.desc: Best model by F-test or AIC comparing one-site vs two-site vs Hill

process: Fit the one-site saturation model (B = Bmax * [L] / (Kd + [L])) by nonlinear regression
Fit the two-site model and the Hill equation as alternatives
Compare models using the extra sum-of-squares F-test or Akaike information criterion
Select the simplest model that adequately describes the data

steps.description: Extract equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) and maximum binding capacity (Bmax) from the best-fit model.

inputs.name: fit-results
inputs.desc: Best model parameters with standard errors

inputs.name: experiment-metadata
inputs.desc: Protein concentration for Bmax per mg calculation

outputs.name: kd-values
outputs.desc: Kd with 95% confidence interval in appropriate units (nM, uM)

outputs.name: bmax-values
outputs.desc: Bmax total and per mg protein with confidence intervals

process: Report Kd from the best-fit model with 95% confidence intervals
Convert Bmax from binding units to fmol/mg or pmol/mg protein using the protein concentration
Verify that Kd falls within the range testable by the ligand concentrations used
Compare Kd to published values for the same receptor-ligand pair if available

steps.description: Analyze competition binding data to determine IC50 and compute Ki using the Cheng-Prusoff equation.

inputs.name: competition-data
inputs.desc: Specific binding of radiolabeled ligand vs concentration of competing compound

inputs.name: kd-values
inputs.desc: Kd of the radiolabeled ligand from saturation analysis

outputs.name: ic50-values
outputs.desc: IC50 for each competing compound with confidence interval

outputs.name: ki-values
outputs.desc: Ki computed from IC50 using the Cheng-Prusoff equation

process: Fit competition curves to the one-site competition model
Extract IC50 from each fitted curve with confidence intervals
Compute Ki = IC50 / (1 + [L]/Kd) using the Cheng-Prusoff equation
Rank competing compounds by Ki from highest to lowest affinity

steps.description: Test for cooperative binding by analyzing Hill coefficient and Scatchard plot linearity.

inputs.name: specific-binding
inputs.desc: Saturation binding data

inputs.name: fit-results
inputs.desc: Hill equation fit parameters including Hill coefficient

outputs.name: cooperativity-assessment
outputs.desc: Hill coefficient interpretation: positive cooperativity (nH > 1), negative (nH < 1), or none (nH = 1)

outputs.name: scatchard-plot
outputs.desc: Scatchard transformation (B/F vs B) showing linearity or curvature

process: Examine the Hill coefficient from the Hill equation fit and its confidence interval
Determine if nH significantly differs from 1 (indicating cooperativity or multiple sites)
Construct the Scatchard plot and assess linearity (linear = one site, curved = complex binding)
Report whether binding is simple, cooperative, or involves heterogeneous sites

steps.description: Compile all binding analysis results into a final receptor pharmacology report.

inputs.name: kd-values
inputs.desc: Equilibrium binding parameters

inputs.name: ki-values
inputs.desc: Competition assay results

inputs.name: cooperativity-assessment
inputs.desc: Cooperativity and binding mechanism conclusions

outputs.name: binding-report
outputs.desc: Final report with saturation curves, Scatchard plots, competition curves, and parameter tables

outputs.name: pharmacology-data
outputs.desc: All raw and fitted data for archival

process: Assemble saturation binding curves, Scatchard plots, and competition curves
Build the parameter summary table (Kd, Bmax, Ki, Hill coefficient) with confidence intervals
Write the interpretation of binding mechanism and receptor pharmacology
Package all raw binding data and fitted parameters for archival
